title: Streaming flow SLOs: client cancellation, incomplete-token reclamation, and backpressure harmonization
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Client-side cancellations, abrupt disconnects, and aggressive timeouts currently leave in-memory generation state (incomplete token streams, reserved KV prefixes, and transient leases) allocated on serving nodes. This increases tail latency for other requests, makes per-customer billing noisy, and occasionally leads to stale structured output / tool call partials being surfaced to clients after reconnects. Goal: Define and implement an SLO-aligned flow control model that reclaims incomplete generation state predictably, surfaces clear signals to SDKs/clients for cancellation vs transient disconnect, and applies consistent backpressure policies across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while preserving structured output consistency and function-call atomicity.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Define and publish a streaming cancellation API contract: graceful-cancel vs force-abort with explicit ack semantics (server returns 200+final-summary or 410 abort marker).
2) Implement a reclamation/lease lifecycle: ephemeral generation leases with configurable grace window (default 30s) and measurable eviction metric (stream.reclaims/sec).
3) KV prefix reservation trimmed on reclaim: prefix TTL removal triggers both cache eviction and any reserved kernel memory release.
4) Backpressure harmonization: token admission controller throttles by per-customer concurrency and sequence-length budget; SLOs preserved within 5% of baseline tail-latency in canary region.
5) SDK compat shim: older SDKs that sent legacy disconnect frames will be mapped to graceful-cancel and receive standardized abort metadata (reason, last-offset) instead of opaque partial text.
6) End-to-end tests cover function-call streaming (tool invocation) behavior on client cancel: either rollback on abort or deliver final partial with structured error envelope.
7) Dashboard: add per-route metrics for orphaned-lease-count, reclaim-latency, and client-cancel-ratio.
8) No regression in existing streaming resume flows for customers with resume tokens enabled (smoketest against ENG-834560).
design_decisions: Lease model: use short lived leases (T_grace configurable, default 30s) instead of immediate hard-abort to allow transient mobile disconnects to rejoin without recomputation.
Cancel semantics: two-level API -- graceful_cancel (server attempts final flush and commits structured output) and force_abort (immediate reclaim, emit abort marker).
Backpressure: admission controller runs per-tenant token-bucket plus adaptive urgency window based on observed latency percentiles (p95/p99).
KV cache handling: on reclaim, issue cache-invalidate for reserved prefixes and schedule kernel free; do not immediately evict shared cache entries unless TTL expired to avoid cache churn.

Function-call streams: preserve atomicity for tool calls -- if graceful_cancel occurs during a tool call, server attempts to finish the tool invocation then attach structured error if incomplete; force_abort cancels invocation and emits structured abort + tool-invocation-aborted flag.
SDK compatibility: implement server-side shim for legacy SDK v1 streaming connect frames that lacked disconnect reason; map to graceful_cancel with reason 'legacy-disconnect' to aid debugging.
Telemetry: new metrics to instrument - stream.lease_allocations, stream.lease_reclaims, stream.graceful_cancel_success, stream.force_abort_count, stream.reclaim_latency_ms.
Rollout strategy: feature-flagged canary in hosted-us-west-2, rollback via feature flag if reclaim latency > 200ms or customer error rate rises > 1%.
Safety: for Private installs, provide config knobs (T_grace, eviction_thresholds) and a migration guide for operators to tune based on GPU workload patterns.
Cost accounting: reclaimed incomplete generations billed as partial_token_units and surfaced in cost breakdown with label 'reclaimed'.
implementation_notes: Server: add LeaseManager component to runtime to track active leases, last-heartbeat, and reclaim pipeline. Store metadata in ephemeral in-memory map with optional durable index for debugging (not required for reclaim semantics).
Admission controller: integrate into existing request router. Add per-tenant quota slot that consumes on first token emit and releases on reclaim or finalization.
Cache: KV cache API extended with 'reserve_prefix' and 'release_prefix' calls; ensure release is idempotent.
SDKs: publish v2.1 streaming client behavior and include example mapping for legacy clients. Update JS/Go/Python SDKs to emit graceful_cancel on close if supported.
Compatibility shim: detect missing disconnect reason header and synthesize 'legacy-disconnect' with best-effort client metadata.
Logs/tracing: emit a structured span when reclaim happens with fields (lease_id, tenant_id, reclaim_reason, reclaimed_bytes, active_tokens).
Metrics: expose Prometheus counters and JSON endpoint for dashboarding; notify cost pipeline for reclaimed token accounting.
Docs: Confluence doc with API examples, recommended grace window by workload, and troubleshooting playbook for reclaimed streams.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable feature-flag in hosted-us-west-2 for 5% of traffic for two days. Monitor stream.reclaim_latency_ms and stream.graceful_cancel_success.
Phase 2 (expanded canary): 25% traffic across two regions for one week, run load tests with synthetic SDK churn pattern (mobile disconnects).
Phase 3 (prod): gradually enable globally over 72 hours with automated rollback if error budget breached.
Private customers: provide operator guide and opt-in boolean; default is off for existing private installs unless they upgrade to runtime-1.21.
Communication: Notify top 20 customers via CSMs before Phase 2; publish breaking-notes for SDK users.
test_plan: Unit tests for LeaseManager reclaim logic and idempotent release_prefix calls.
Integration tests: simulate network flaps and client cancel scenarios, assert reclaim happens within configured T_grace and admission tokens are released.
E2E: function-call streaming test harness verifying tool invocation atomicity on graceful_cancel vs force_abort.
Chaos test: inject delayed reclaim and measure downstream latency impact to validate admission controller protects tail latency.
Compatibility tests: run legacy SDKs to confirm synthesize reason mapping and appropriate client-surface metadata.
updates: 2026-03-02: Design review with Runtime and SDK leads. Decided on two-tier cancel API and default grace window of 30s. Action: Liam to prototype LeaseManager.
2026-03-04: Prototype LeaseManager done. Observed reclamation spike causing small CPU jitter in microbenchmarks; mitigated by batching reclaim operations into 50ms windows.
2026-03-06: Added idempotent release_prefix to KV cache API. QA to validate race with concurrent finalization and reclaim.
2026-03-08: PRs opened (see links). Console dashboard draft created; awaiting metrics pipeline changes (ENG-412908 dependency).
2026-03-10: Canary toggle staged in us-west-2; synthetic churn test scheduled for 2026-03-11. No customer-facing docs yet; draft in confluence.
notes: Trade-offs: longer grace windows reduce recompute for flaky clients but increase memory pressure; we picked a conservative default (30s) and expose tuning knobs.
Consideration: hard-abort on overload instead of reclaim to free memory faster — rejected due to structured output consistency requirements for tool calls.
Follow-ups: metric to correlate reclaimed tokens with billing anomalies (next ticket), and a UX in console to surface active lease counts per-customer.
Related tickets: ENG-834560 (resume flows), ENG-412908 (dashboard metrics pipeline).
